contents: 1: Master Your Emotional Self — The Law of Irrationality
2: Transform Self-Love into Empathy — The Law of Narcissism
3: See Through People's Masks — The Law of Role-playing
4: Determine the Strength of People's Character — The Law of Compulsive Behavior
5: Become an Elusive Object of Desire — The Law of Covetousness
6: Elevate Your Perspective — The Law of Shortsightedness
7: Soften People's Resistance by Confirming Their Self-opinion — The Law of Defensiveness
8: Change Your Circumstances by Changing Your Attitude — The Law of Self-sabotage
9: Confront Your Dark Side — The Law of Repression
10: Beware the Fragile Ego — The Law of Envy
11: Know Your Limits — The Law of Grandiosity
12: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You — The Law of Gender Rigidity
13: Advance with a Sense of Purpose — The Law of Aimlessness
14: Resist the Downward Pull of the Group — The Law of Conformity
15: Make Them Want to Follow You — The Law of Fickleness
16: See the Hostility Behind the Friendly Façade — The Law of Aggression
17: Seize the Historical Moment — The Law of Generational Myopia
18: Meditate on Our Common Mortality — The Law of Death Denial

audiences: Readers who want a broad vocabulary for recurring social and emotional patterns
Managers, founders, and negotiators who learn from historical case studies
People interested in self-observation, character, group behaviour, power, and purpose
Robert Greene readers who want the psychological assumptions behind his strategy books

sources.title: The Laws of Human Nature
sources.supports: US edition metadata, formats, audiobook duration, synopsis, author credit, and selected professional review excerpts.
sources.limitations: Authoritative for publication facts but promotional in its description of quality and expertise.

sources.title: The Laws of Human Nature: publisher preview
sources.supports: Copyright, contents, introduction, opening argument, structure, voice, and the start of the Law of Irrationality.
sources.limitations: A 23-page preview, not the complete 624-page book.

sources.title: The Laws of Human Nature
sources.supports: Hardcover identity, publication date, ISBN, length, selected contents, searchable passages, index terms, and references.
sources.limitations: Limited preview with uneven access across chapters.

sources.title: Robert Greene: The Laws of Human Nature
sources.supports: Greene's explanation of detachment from emotion, intrinsic motives, self-control, empathy, and the purpose of the book.
sources.limitations: An author talk and interview, not independent validation of the laws.

sources.title: The Laws of Human Nature
sources.supports: Positive professional assessment of organisation, historical cases, major examples, the step-back message, and the book's reflective value.
sources.limitations: A concise review that does not audit the scientific basis of all eighteen laws.

sources.title: The Laws of Human Nature
sources.supports: Critical professional assessment of the book's pessimistic frame, formula, truisms, long illustrative stories, inflated claims, and information efficiency.
sources.limitations: One strongly negative review with an intentionally sharp editorial voice.

sources.title: The Laws of Human Nature
sources.supports: Independent overview of the book's use of philosophers, psychologists, writers, and representative laws, plus bibliographic details.
sources.limitations: Brief collection-development review with little detailed criticism; page was accessible through search indexing only.

sources.title: The Laws of Human Nature
sources.supports: Large reader aggregate and recurring praise for breadth and historical illustration alongside criticism of anecdotal selection, repetition, and overclaiming.
sources.limitations: Self-selected ratings, possible edition merging, and no control for completion or reader expertise.

sources.title: The Laws of Human Nature: book summary
sources.supports: Cross-check of all eighteen law titles, the five-part organisation, historical examples, and practical recommendations.
sources.limitations: Commercial condensation that paraphrases and reorganises the book; only two laws are treated deeply in the free version.

sources.title: The Laws of Human Nature summary and study guide
sources.supports: Chapter-by-chapter account based on a 2018 Penguin edition, major historical figures, themes, and the full progression of eighteen laws.
sources.limitations: A commercial study guide and secondary interpretation, used with primary and independent corroboration.

workflow.coverage_notes: Checked the publisher preview and searchable Google Books edition, then triangulated every law and major historical example through two detailed chapter treatments, the author's long-form talk, and independent professional and reader reception. The complete book was not available as one uninterrupted lawful text, so the profile does not claim full-book verification.
next_steps: Optional: compare every historical case and endnote with an owner-supplied or library copy to raise coverage to full-book.
